source_text:
Uerumtamen si ita est, adparet terram tenebrarum a terra lucis duobus lateribus tangi; et utique si duobus tangitur, duobus etiam tangit. certe iuxta unum latus erat terra tenebrarum.
Deinde quam foeda figura terrae lucis adparet. tamquam fissa ungula nigro quodam cuneo subter artato, iliac tantum finita. qua finditur. hians etiam et patens desuper interposito inani, quicquid a superficie terrae tenebrarum sursum uersus inmensum est. quam deinde melior ipsius terrae tenebrarum figura ostenditur, si quidem illa findit. haec finditur; illa inseritur, haec interpatet: illa in se nulli inanitati dat locum. haec ab inferiore tantum parte laxa non est, qua hostili cuneo subinpletur. indocti ergo homines et auari cum maiorem honorem tribuunt multitudini partium quam unitati. ut sex partes darent terrae lucis, tres deorsum uersus. tres sursum uersus, maluerunt penetrari terram lucis quam penetrare. tali enim figura etsi conmixtam negant. penetratam tamen negare non possunt.
thought_title: The land of light is penetrated by the land of darkness
orientation: Augustine continues his spatial critique of Mani's two eternal lands, now showing that the land of darkness touches and penetrates the land of light on two sides.
pass_a_gloss: But if it is so, it appears that the land of darkness is touched by the land of light on two sides; and certainly if it is touched on two sides, it also touches on two sides. Certainly the land of darkness was along one side. Then how foul a shape of the land of light appears. Like a split hoof with a black wedge pressed in beneath, finite only on that side where it is split. Also gaping and open above with emptiness placed between, whatever is immense upward from the surface of the land of darkness. Then how much better the shape of the land of darkness itself is shown, if indeed that one splits, this one is split; that one is inserted, this one lies open between: that one gives place in itself to no emptiness, this one is not loose only from the lower part, where it is filled up beneath by the hostile wedge. Therefore unlearned and greedy men, when they give greater honor to the multitude of parts than to unity, so that they gave six parts to the land of light, three downward, three upward, preferred the land of light to be penetrated than to penetrate. For with such a shape, even if they deny it is mixed, they cannot deny it is penetrated.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for Mani's realm of evil.
Fixed glossary term for Mani's realm of God.
Renders the void space Augustine says Mani places above the land of darkness; 'emptiness' keeps the spatial sense.
Augustine's key charge: the land of light is pierced by the land of darkness; 'penetrated' preserves the spatial and hostile force.
Keeps the causal 'ergo' and the two adjectives as a single pejorative description of the Manichaeans.

choices.english: to the multitude of parts than to unity
choices.why: Literal rendering of the comparison; Augustine contrasts many parts with oneness.
rejected: to many parts rather than to oneness
to the number of parts over unity

pass_b_english: But if that is so, it appears that the land of darkness is touched by the land of light on two sides; and certainly if it is touched on two sides, it also touches on two sides. At any rate, the land of darkness lay along one side.

Then how ugly the shape of the land of light appears: like a split hoof with a black wedge pressed in beneath it, bounded only on the side where it is split, while above it gapes open with emptiness between, immense as it is from the surface of the land of darkness upward. How much better, then, the shape of the land of darkness itself is shown to be, since the one splits and the other is split; the one is inserted and the other lies open between; the one gives no place within itself to any emptiness, while the other is compact only on its lower side, where the hostile wedge fills it from beneath. Therefore unlearned and greedy men, since they give greater honor to the multitude of parts than to unity—so as to give six parts to the land of light, three downward and three upward—preferred that the land of light be penetrated rather than penetrate. For with such a shape, even if they deny it was mixed, they cannot deny it was penetrated.

problems.quote: the one splits and the other is split
problems.why: Reverses agency: illa (land of light) splits, haec (land of darkness) is split
problems.fix: the one splits, the other is split
problems.ruling: 'illa findit, haec finditur': illa=light splits, haec=darkness is split; English reverses with 'one splits, other is split'.

problems.quote: the one is inserted and the other lies open between
problems.why: Reverses agency: illa (land of light) is inserted, haec (land of darkness) lies open between
problems.fix: the one is inserted, the other lies open between
problems.ruling: 'illa inseritur, haec interpatet': illa=light is inserted, haec=darkness lies open; English reverses referents.

problems.quote: the other is not loose only on its lower side
problems.source_quote: haec ab inferiore tantum parte laxa non est
problems.why: Wrong negation scope: 'laxa non est' means 'is not loose,' not 'not loose only'
problems.fix: the other is not loose on its lower side only
problems.ruling: 'tantum parte' modifies lower side; 'laxa non est' = 'is not loose'; English 'not loose only' wrongly scopes negation.

edits.old: the one splits and the other is split; the one is inserted and the other lies open between; the one gives no place within itself to any emptiness, while the other is not loose only on its lower side
edits.new: the one is split and the other splits; the one lies open between and the other is inserted; the one gives no place within itself to any emptiness, while the other is not loose on its lower side only

fixed: Reversed agency in 'the one splits and the other is split': source 'illa findit. haec finditur' has illa (land of light) splitting, haec (land of darkness) being split.
Reversed agency in 'the one is inserted and the other lies open between': source 'illa inseritur, haec interpatet' has illa (land of light) being inserted, haec (land of darkness) lying open between.

Wrong negation scope in 'the other is not loose only on its lower side': source 'haec ab inferiore tantum parte laxa non est' means 'is not loose on its lower side only,' not 'not loose only on its lower side.'

problems.quote: while above it gapes open with emptiness between—everything from the surface of the land of darkness upward is immense
problems.source_quote: hians etiam et patens desuper interposito inani, quicquid a superficie terrae tenebrarum sursum uersus inmensum est
problems.why: Misreads syntax: 'inmensum est' describes the emptiness, not 'everything upward'
problems.fix: gaping open above with emptiness between, immense as it is from the surface of the land of darkness upward

problems.quote: the other is not loose on its lower side only
problems.source_quote: haec ab inferiore tantum parte laxa non est
problems.why: Wrong negation scope: 'tantum...non' = 'only on the lower side is it not loose', not 'not loose on lower side only'
problems.fix: the other is not loose only on its lower side

problems.quote: the one lies open between and the other is inserted
problems.why: Subjects are reversed: 'illa' (land of darkness) is inserted, 'haec' (land of light) lies open between.
problems.fix: the one is inserted and the other lies open between
problems.ruling: 'illa' refers to darkness (fem. abl.), 'haec' to light; translator reversed subjects.

edits.old: while above it gapes open with emptiness between—everything from the surface of the land of darkness upward is immense
edits.new: while above it gapes open with emptiness between, immense as it is from the surface of the land of darkness upward

edits.old: the other is not loose on its lower side only
edits.new: the other is not loose only on its lower side

edits.old: the one lies open between and the other is inserted
edits.new: the one is inserted and the other lies open between

fixed: Corrected the syntax of 'hians etiam et patens desuper interposito inani, quicquid a superficie terrae tenebrarum sursum uersus inmensum est': 'inmensum est' describes the emptiness, not everything upward.
Corrected the negation scope of 'haec ab inferiore tantum parte laxa non est': 'only on the lower side is it not loose'.
Corrected the reversed subjects in 'illa inseritur, haec interpatet': 'illa' (land of darkness) is inserted, 'haec' (land of light) lies open between.

problems.quote: the one is split and the other splits
problems.why: The land of darkness splits and the land of light is split. English reverses the two.
problems.fix: since the one splits and the other is split; the one is inserted and the other lies open between
problems.ruling: "illa findit, haec finditur": illa is the dark land, which splits, and haec is the light land, which is split. The English reverses them and contradicts its own later "the other lies open".

edits.old: since the one is split and the other splits; the one is inserted and the other lies open between
edits.new: since the one splits and the other is split; the one is inserted and the other lies open between

fixed: Reversed split-pair: source 'illa findit, haec finditur' (with 'illa inseritur, haec interpatet') has darkness splitting/inserted and light split/lying open, so changed to 'the one splits and the other is split'.

problems.quote: the other is not loose only on its lower side, where it is filled up beneath by the hostile wedge
problems.source_quote: haec ab inferiore tantum parte laxa non est, qua hostili cuneo subinpletur
problems.why: English “not loose only” reads as loose in more places than the bottom. Latin: it is tight only below, where the wedge fills it.
problems.fix: while the other is compact only on its lower side, where the hostile wedge fills it from beneath
problems.ruling: Latin "laxa non est" = not loose/open only below; English "not loose only on its lower side" is ambiguous and suggests loose elsewhere, inverting emphasis of "ab inferiore tantum parte".

edits.old: while the other is not loose only on its lower side, where it is filled up beneath by the hostile wedge
edits.new: while the other is compact only on its lower side, where the hostile wedge fills it from beneath

fixed: Fixed lower-side clause: Latin 'haec ab inferiore tantum parte laxa non est, qua hostili cuneo subinpletur' means tight/compact only below, not loose elsewhere — changed to 'compact only on its lower side'.

last_rejected.quote: while above it gapes open with emptiness between, immense as it is from the surface of the land of darkness upward
last_rejected.source_quote: hians etiam et patens desuper interposito inani, quicquid a superficie terrae tenebrarum sursum uersus inmensum est
last_rejected.why: English inverts spatial relation: source says land of light gapes open above with emptiness between, whatever is immense upward from surface of darkness; English makes 'immense' modify wrong thing and obscures that emptiness fills space from darkness's surface upward.
last_rejected.fix: gaping open above with emptiness between, however immense the space upward from the surface of the land of darkness
last_rejected.ruling: English conveys same spatial sense: gapes above with emptiness, immense upward from darkness surface. Minor phrasing, not meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: the one gives no place within itself to any emptiness
last_rejected.source_quote: illa in se nulli inanitati dat locum
last_rejected.why: English 'within itself' misrepresents 'in se' which means 'in itself' (i.e., the land of darkness itself contains no emptiness), not 'within itself' as interior space; also 'illa' refers to darkness, not light, but English 'the one' is ambiguous.
last_rejected.fix: the one gives no place in itself to any emptiness
last_rejected.ruling: 'Within itself' is normal rendering of 'in se'; 'the one/other' pattern tracks illa/haec correctly. No real error.

last_rejected.quote: while the other is not loose only on its lower side
last_rejected.source_quote: haec ab inferiore tantum parte laxa non est
last_rejected.why: English 'not loose only' is garbled; source means 'this one is not open/unbounded only on its lower side' (i.e., it's also open above where the wedge enters). 'Laxa' means open/unconfined, not 'loose'.
last_rejected.fix: while the other is not open only on its lower side
last_rejected.ruling: 'Not loose only on lower side' captures 'laxa non est tantum'; 'loose' within range for 'laxa'. Meaning preserved adequately.

last_rejected.quote: preferred that the land of light be penetrated rather than penetrate
last_rejected.source_quote: maluerunt penetrari terram lucis quam penetrare
last_rejected.why: English omits agent of penetration; source means they preferred that land of light be penetrated [by darkness] rather than [land of light] penetrate [darkness]. English 'penetrate' without object is unclear.
last_rejected.fix: preferred that the land of light be penetrated rather than that it penetrate
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'penetrare' is also intransitive here; English mirrors source structure. Ambiguity exists in both, not a mistranslation.
